text:
matt: Quick heads-up — on the Go SDK onboarding sample app, streaming generators behave weirdly when you cancel ctx mid-emit. Repro steps attached.

julia: can you paste the minimal repro here?

matt: Sure: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
gen := client.Generator(ctx, req)
go func(){
  time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
  cancel()
}()
for tok := range gen.Next(){
  fmt.Println(tok)
}
``` After cancel, goroutine sometimes blocks in Next() forever. Not consistent.

sarah: Hmm, similar to a leak we saw but not identical. Is your gen.Next() returning channel or iterator? Any error val?

matt: It's an iterator that yields (string, error). On cancel, sometimes error==context.Canceled, other times it blocks. The handshake shows the initial HTTP/2 stream remains open.

ken: Does this happen with auth refresh in flight? We had a bug where auth refresh retries re-attach and left the read loop waiting.

matt: I disabled token-refresh and it still happened.

julia: Can you run with GODEBUG=net/http2=1 to get logs? Also which server (hosted vs local) and model?

matt: Hosted dev region, redwood-go v0.12.1, model: rwd-13b-v1.0. Logs: [paste] "transport: failed to read frame: read tcp ...: use of closed network connection" then nothing.

devex-bot: @matt thanks — filed as DE-7843: "go-sdk-generator-ctx-cancel-iterator-block" assigned to eng-runtime.

sarah: From reading runtime notes, generator uses long-lived stream + partial frames; cancel should close conn and signal iterator. Could be race where cancel closes context after next() checked for closed state but before read loop selects.

ken: Proposal: change iterator.Next() to select on ctx.Done() before blocking on recv; also make internal read loop set a terminal error on iterator on any transport close.

julia: Sounds good. For onboarding docs: we should add a snippet demonstrating proper cancel pattern: show defer cancel in caller and a for loop that checks err != nil and breaks. Add a note about auth-refresh causing transient hang.

matt: I'll open a small sample app PR that reproduces and a second PR for the fix proposal. PR will include failing test using a mocked transport.

julia: Great — can you tag me and @sarah in PR? :thumbsup: 

matt: Will do. Quick note: could we add a short "Streaming gotchas" section in the Go quickstart? I think many users hit this.

julia: Agreed. Add an FAQ entry and link to DE-7843 tracker.

ken: Also add a linter rule to warn if generator returned iterator isn't consumed with context or timeout — might be heavy-handed though.

sarah: Maybe just add examples and emphasize patterns: close/cancel, use select with ctx.Done, and timeouts.

matt: Filed PRs: 4567 (repro sample), 4568 (iterator fix). Tagging thread when merged.

devex-bot: PR 4567 and 4568 referenced in DE-7843.
